title: Cost-Sensitive Stacking: an Empirical Evaluation
reasoning: The paper focuses on cost-sensitive classification and ensemble methods, evaluating different stacking setups based on misclassification costs. While these applications (e.g., in medicine, credit scoring) inherently have ethical implications regarding fairness and impact, the paper itself does not benchmark or evaluate the models specifically on ethical or moral principles, nor does it discuss religion or faith. Its scope is the empirical performance of cost-sensitive machine learning techniques.
